idiom_name: Hash of procs/lambdas (+ Object#public_send for method-name rules) republished under a Mutex
implementation_notes: Ruby's dispatch table is a Hash from key to callable, or from key to a method name invoked with public_send, which goes through normal method lookup and refuses private methods (unlike send). The control channel is conventionally a signal (SIGUSR1) or a reader thread that republishes the table; replace the whole frozen Hash under a Mutex rather than mutating entries in place, because Hash#[]= is atomic per key but a multi-rule update is not visible as one generation. Freeze published tables so an accidental rule edit fails loudly instead of mutating live routing.
pitfalls: send bypasses method visibility and happily calls private methods; use public_send for any method name that comes from a rule.
A frozen Hash raises FrozenError on writes - freeze deliberately so a stray rule edit fails loudly instead of mutating live routing state.
Signal handlers run in a restricted context: allocations and locking inside a trap can raise ThreadError, so hand the reload to a queue and republish from a thread.

variants.name: Rails route set rebuilt at runtime
variants.idiom_name: Rails.application.routes.draw + reload_routes! / mounted Rack rule router
variants.implementation_notes: In a Rails application the router is the framework's: routes declared with Rails.application.routes.draw map verb plus path to a controller action, the route set is a runtime object that can be rebuilt with Rails.application.reload_routes! (or by calling draw again) so route changes land without a restart, and constraints (lambda or request-based) turn message content into a matching condition. Route order is significant because the first matching route wins, and a mounted Rack application is the escape hatch for destinations that are not controllers - including a rule-base router of its own. Use this realization for request-shaped traffic inside a Rails app; for in-process dispatch keep the Hash table.
variants.code_sketch:
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get  "/orders/:id", to: "orders#show"
  post "/orders",     to: "orders#create"
  mount TenantRouter.new(rule_base), at: "/tenants"   # runtime rule base
end

# control channel: rebuild the route set without restarting the app
Rails.application.reload_routes!
pitfalls: Route order is first-match-wins, so a broad route added by a rule update can shadow the specific routes declared after it.
reload_routes! rebuilds the URL helpers too; code holding old helpers keeps generating stale paths.
Calling draw at runtime from several threads mutates global router state - serialize rule updates, or prefer a mounted Rack app for genuinely dynamic per-tenant routing.
